repository_commit_line_104_finding.reasoning: cuda-preflight.sh:104 (the 'repository_commit=' line inside the environment.txt heredoc block) runs unconditionally, well before the old :544 CANDIDATE_SHA= line. On a no-.git remote, the script would have died there regardless of any fix at :544 -- the design doc itself says this explicitly ('the script dies at its first call there', i.e. :104 first). Fixing only :544 would have been necessary but not sufficient for AC80-22's real-run requirement. I resolved CANDIDATE_SHA once, early (right after sourcing the new lib, before any other preflight work), and changed the :104 line to print that already-resolved value (printf 'repository_commit=%s\n' "$CANDIDATE_SHA") instead of shelling out to git a second time. This is stricter than doing two independent resolutions: it guarantees repository_commit= in the evidence and candidate_sha in the witness can never disagree, and it fails fast (before touching Docker/model-cache/GPU) on an invalid FATHOMDB_CANDIDATE_SHA rather than failing deep into the run. Byte-identical output preserved for the git-present/unset-var path since 'git rev-parse HEAD' via command substitution strips the trailing newline the same way either call site would.

shellcheck_finding_and_fix.what_happened: scripts/agent-lint-shell.sh's shell-early-consumer guard (scripts/lib/shell-early-consumer.sh) flagged my first draft of resolve_cuda_candidate_sha: `printf '%s' "$FATHOMDB_CANDIDATE_SHA" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{40}$'` is exactly the producer-piped-into-early-exiting-consumer-under-pipefail hazard the guard exists to catch.
shellcheck_finding_and_fix.fix: Replaced the printf|grep pipeline with bash's own regex match: `[[ "$FATHOMDB_CANDIDATE_SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]`, matching existing house precedent for exactly this kind of 40-hex-SHA check (scripts/verify-release-gates.sh:82: `[[ "$candidate" =~ ^[0-9A-Fa-f]{40}$ ]]`). No pipe, no subshell, no SIGPIPE hazard.
